firstScreen.notes: 1440-first.jpg: h1 'Formosan termites in New Orleans' names pest + city in 5 words but no outcome; phone in header and secondary button; proof line is 3 lines of mono with a hyphen range '$275-$475/per year'. The right half is a flat beige rectangle (placeholder media), so the hero reads unfinished. Concept promised family 4 (stacked headline over a 21:9 dusk strip); delivered a stock split 'text left, photo right'. Empty dark band under the hero, nothing peeks (-0.5). ZIP field adds a third action next to two buttons. 390-first.jpg: h1 2 lines, both actions above fold, phone icon in header: good.

distinctiveness.notes: The dusk-clock is visible only as a 48px circle in the hero (1440-first.jpg, 390-first.jpg). Story, reviews and footer carry the hook attribute but no visible clock, time stamps or dimming lamp (1440-scroll-25.jpg, 1440-scroll-75.jpg, 1440-rm-full.jpg): signature only in the hero (-2.0). Mono tracked eyebrow over every heading ('WHAT WE DO', 'SAMPLE PRICES', 'FROM REAL PORCHES', 1440-scroll-50.jpg, 1440-scroll-75.jpg) (-0.5). The 3x3 bordered service-card grid with a 'Price it' link on each is a template shape (1440-scroll-50.jpg) (-0.5). Palette and serif do differ from pest-A (light green slab, sites/pest/A/qa/screens/1440-first.jpg).

type.notes: EB Garamond display + Karla body + DM Mono accent is a good pairing and the italic Garamond review quotes are the best type on the page (1440-scroll-75.jpg). Straight quotes on every review and a hyphen price range in the hero proof line (1440-scroll-75.jpg, 1440-first.jpg) (-0.5). The mono is overused: kicker, proof line, review meta, rating, prices, so 3+ tracked caps labels share one view (1440-scroll-75.jpg). There is no scale-contrast moment beyond the h1.

layout.notes: The tone order works: indigo hero, blue-hour helper, midnight story, full-bleed break, indigo services, parchment prices, midnight reviews, gold guarantee band (1440-rm-full.jpg). But each of the four house-type cards is a ~700px bordered box holding one image and two lines, with the right column and the bottom third empty (1440-scroll-25.jpg) (-0.5 for blank space; the story runs four screens for one idea). The 1440 hero leaves the bottom ~100px empty with no peek (1440-first.jpg). Services, prices and reviews all use the same left-heading-over-grid shape (1440-rm-full.jpg) (-0.5).

photo.notes: Every frame on the page is a flat beige rectangle: hero, the four story cards, the full-bleed break and the area image (1440-first.jpg, 1440-scroll-25.jpg, 1440-scroll-50.jpg, 1440-rm-full.jpg, 390-rm-full.jpg). The dist/media files are all byte-identical 16,907-byte placeholders. There is no grade, no crop and no subject. The alt text describes photos that are not there ('Row of shotgun houses at blue hour', and the file is 'home-wilmington.jpg', a different city's name). Below the floor; a builder cannot fix this alone.

copy.notes: Specific and in a local voice: 'Swarmers gather at dusk from late April through June', 'Brick-between-posts with a side hall. We check the wood sills, the attic access and the crawlspace vents' (1440-first.jpg, 1440-scroll-25.jpg). The reviews kicker 'From real porches' sits over reviews labelled Sample and claims they are real (1440-scroll-75.jpg): mustFix, capped at 8. 'Price it' repeats nine times (1440-scroll-50.jpg). The estimator shows 'Sample yearly range: —' before any input (1440-scroll-75.jpg).

mobile.notes: 390-first.jpg: designed and not just collapsed; h1 2 lines, stacked full-width actions, ZIP inline. 390-rm-full.jpg: story cards stack, no sideways scroll (render.json overflow clean at 320/390), a call bar is present. The native checkboxes and radios in the plan builder and lights-out helper are about 13px targets (1440-scroll-75.jpg, 390-rm-full.jpg) (-0.5). The hero placeholder sits below the fold, so the phone first screen has no image at all.

a11y.notes: 1440-rm-full.jpg and 390-rm-full.jpg show every section and every word. The clock is aria-hidden, and there is one h1 with ordered h2/h3. Native checkboxes are tiny and unstyled for focus on the parchment band (1440-scroll-75.jpg). The motion-on full shots (1440-full.jpg, 390-full.jpg) show prices, reviews, area and contact blank until reveal; the scroll-75 frame shows they appear, so this is not a mustFix, but the reveal starts at opacity 0 for whole sections.

motion.notes: Hooks in dist/index.html: h1 line split, data-reveal, hotspots, and a clock hand rotated by --sw-p. Nothing in the 25/50/75 frames shows the promised story: no advancing clock, no porch light dimming, no pin state (1440-scroll-25.jpg shows plain stacked cards). Whole sections fade in the same way (1440-full.jpg blank bands) (-1.0 for the same reveal everywhere).

wow.notes: The thesis 'the page darkens as dusk passes' does not show on screen: tones are fixed, and the clock is a 48px dial in one corner (1440-first.jpg). The lights-out helper and plan builder output plain text lines ('Sample yearly range: —', 1440-scroll-75.jpg) (-1.0). Nothing here a homeowner would show their partner.

polish.notes: SVG favicon, apple-touch, OG 1200x630, print and forced-colors blocks are present (dist/index.html). Mixed radius: pill 'Sample rating' badge against square buttons and cards (1440-scroll-75.jpg) (-0.5). The backdrop-filter glass disc behind the hero clock (1440-first.jpg) is a slop tell. The page ships with placeholder frames, so it cannot look finished at any viewport.

mustFix.problem: All seven images are identical 16,907-byte beige placeholders. The site has no photography.
mustFix.fix: Re-run media curation for niches/pest (real approved library, with distinct files per slot), then rebuild. Escalate to the orchestrator: niche media is not approved in any real sense.

mustFix.problem: The kicker 'From real porches' calls Sample reviews real, which breaks demo honesty.
mustFix.fix: Replace with 'Sample porches' or 'Sample reviews, New Orleans' and keep the Sample rating badge.

elevate.move: Once real frames exist, grade every one into the indigo/streetlamp duotone and cut the hero as the promised 21:9 dusk strip under the stacked headline, so the photography itself is the dusk window and not boxes beside text.

Make the dusk clock the page's spine: a fixed clock in the margin whose hand and the section ground both advance from 7:40 to 9:30 pm through the story, reviews stamped with times on that clock, and the footer landing at 9:30 with the lamp glow down to a hairline.
